extracted.intended_audience: prose fiction writers / creative writers seeking craft instruction
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and revising prose fiction focused on sound, syntax, POV, exposition, and word choice, with practical exercises to build technique and discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Sound of Your Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Prose rhythm, musicality, onomatopoeia, alliteration; avoid 'dull, choppy, droning' prose; aim for 'flowing, strong' prose through perfect placement and timing of words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listen for rhythm—read aloud. Use onomatopoeia, alliteration, invented words and rhythmic effects without resorting to rhyme or strict meter. Sound problems are often the cause of weak prose; exercise: write a paragraph intended for reading aloud emphasizing sonic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation and Grammar as Craft Tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat punctuation and grammar not merely as rules but as deliberate stylistic and structural tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use punctuation and grammatical choices to shape pacing, emphasis, and tone. Consider nonstandard or subtle punctuation choices when they serve voice or rhythm; avoid seeing rules only as constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence Length and Complex Syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Vary sentence length and control syntactic complexity to manage pace and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate variety prevents monotony; control complexity so meaning remains clear. Use long sentences for flow or accumulation and short sentences for emphasis or impact; balance is key.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition (Strategic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Intentional repetition can create rhythm and emphasis when used purposefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between lazy repetition and deliberate refrains. Use repeated words, phrases, or structures to build pattern or resonance, but avoid unthinking duplication that dulls prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjectives and Adverbs (Economy of Modifiers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid lazy modifiers (e.g., 'suddenly', 'somehow'); prefer stronger verbs and nouns to create vividness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh each modifier: identify which are 'Styrofoam' (flimsy, unnecessary) and which are 'heavy gold' (essential). Exercise: write 200–350 words without adjectives or adverbs (except time-related) to force stronger word choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verbs: Person and Tense
rubrics_metrics.description: Choices of tense and grammatical person affect the reader's experience of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select tense and person to align with intimacy, immediacy, and narrative distance. Be consistent unless deliberate shifts are justified; test different combinations to see how they change the story's effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of View and Voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide between single-character limited, multi-character limited, or an involved/detached author voice to shape narrative perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match POV choice to the story's needs for intimacy and information. Voice (tone, diction, narrative persona) should be coherent with chosen POV; use examples from the canon to study effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing Point of View
rubrics_metrics.description: When shifting POVs, manage transitions carefully—signal changes and control head-hopping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear chapter/section breaks, narrative signals, or perspective anchors to avoid confusing the reader. Occasional controlled head-hopping can be effective but must be signaled and purposeful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Narration / Crowding and Leaping
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide what to include versus omit; determine what to dramatize and what to summarize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid crowding scenes with unnecessary detail and avoid leaping over moments that should be dramatized. Choose when to show (scene) and when to tell (summary) for pacing and clarity; trim extraneous information.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Expository Lump (Invisible Exposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid heavy-handed exposition that interrupts the narrative 'dream'; integrate background and explanation invisibly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dialogue, setting details, and action to convey necessary information. Anti-patterns: lecture-like exposition or info dumps. Exercises: create dialogue-only scenes or environmental details that reveal character/history without overt explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise: Hearing the Sound of Your Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Write one paragraph to one page meant for reading aloud using onomatopoeia, alliteration, rhythmic effects, and invented words but no rhyme or meter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: train sensitivity to sonic texture. Constraint (no rhyme/meter) forces attention to natural prose rhythm and word placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise: Eliminate Adjectives & Adverbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Write 200–350 words of descriptive narrative without adjectives or adverbs (except time-related). Use only verbs, nouns, pronouns, and articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: force reliance on strong verbs and nouns; reveal which modifiers are essential vs. flabby. This exposes 'Styrofoam' modifiers and trains economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise: Master Invisible Exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Create scenes that convey information without explicit exposition—examples include dialogue-only scenes revealing character, settings revealing absent characters, and scenes where complex processes unfold through conversation/action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice embedding necessary background and complexity inside action and speech. Avoid 'lecturing' the reader; make exposition feel like part of the lived scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention and Self-discipline (Writing as Learnable Craft)
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing requires practice, focus, and discipline rather than reliance solely on innate talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular practice through exercises and revision is emphasized. The writer should treat craft as learnable and apply steady work to improve technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid Sensory Rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: Prose should have vivid sensory detail and a strong internal rhythm that engages readers' senses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete sensory description and rhythmic sentence choices to immerse the reader; sound and sensory detail work together to create presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy ('Styrofoam' vs 'Heavy Gold')
rubrics_metrics.description: Trim unnecessary words and retain only elements that carry weight; identify which words are flabby versus essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh language by forcing cuts or constraints to reveal what must remain. Prefer fewer, stronger words; eliminate filler that dulls prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Should Integrate, Never Interrupt the Dream
rubrics_metrics.description: Background and necessary information must be blended into the narrative flow so they don't disrupt immersion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for 'invisible' delivery of exposition; avoid passages that pull the reader out of the story to explain. Test by removing explicit exposition and finding ways to imply facts through scene, action, and detail.
